title: EPFO Cannot Reject Higher-Pension Joint Options by Citing an Exempted Establishment's PF Trust Rules: Bombay High Court
case_name: Amit Gunvantrai Mehta & Ors. v. Employees' Provident Fund Organisation & Ors.
card_summary: Justice Sandeep V. Marne set aside EPFO's rejection of higher-pension joint-option applications by employees of exempted establishments, where EPFO relied on the establishment's own PF trust rules capping contributions at the statutory wage ceiling. The court held those rules cannot override an employee's statutory right to higher pension, and ordered EPFO to process the six applications within eight weeks.
card_tip: An exempted establishment's PF trust rules on contribution ceilings do not by themselves defeat an employee's higher-pension joint option; a rejection on that ground alone is worth challenging.
verification_notes: Outlook Money, The Law Communicants and Law Trend agree on the judge (Justice Sandeep V. Marne), the 19 October 2026 date, the six writ petitions, the holding on PF trust rules versus the statutory joint option, and the eight-week processing direction. None of the three gives a citation number; full judgment not independently reviewed.
